findings.title: Grant shortcut check in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses wrong substring indices and inverted condition
findings.body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs: (1) in the 6-character prefix `<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>` (e.g. `onrtac`), the 2-character grant type shortcut is at indices 4..6 (`substring(4, 6)`), whereas `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"`); and (2) the `.equals(...)` check is not negated, so it returns `false` on a match and continues on a mismatch. Because `substring(3, 5)` never equals valid grant shortcuts like `"ac"` or `"rt"`, the condition is always `false` and the matcher erroneously passes without verifying the grant type shortcut. It should check `items[0].length() == 6` and `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`.

findings.title: Null check in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`, checking `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. Passing a `null` `rawTokenId` will not be rejected at construction time.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() Javadoc specifies 3-letter shortcuts but encoder requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` does not validate shortcut length. However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the entire encoded context prefix to be 6 characters (`encodedContext.length() != 6`) and slices the grant shortcut from indices 4 to 6 (`encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). Any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut will produce encoded token IDs that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException instead of testing IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`, `before()` does not call `factory.postInit(...)`, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` as `null`. When `testIncorrectGrantType()` calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")` with the unregistered shortcut `"ac"`, `factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` attempts to call `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException`, which is caught by `catch (RuntimeException iae)`. Consequently, the `IllegalArgumentException` branch in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` for an unknown grant type shortcut is never reached.
